subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw keep automatic final text as the channel default while suppressing only internal/inter-tool text, or move channel-visible output toward explicit message-tool sends by default?
rationale: The security goal is clear, but the documented automatic reply default is a compatibility contract for existing channel users, so automation should not choose the new default policy alone.

options.title: Preserve automatic finals, suppress internals
options.body: Keep intentional final assistant text deliverable by default, but suppress commentary, reasoning, unphased pre-tool/inter-tool text, and cron reasoning payloads with focused source and channel regression tests.

options.title: Require explicit message sends
options.body: Make channel-visible output require message(action=send) by default, accepting a larger compatibility break for a stronger security boundary.

options.title: Ship opt-in mitigations only
options.body: Land the open opt-in or narrow PRs without changing defaults, leaving affected users protected only after configuration changes.

recommendation.title: Preserve automatic finals, suppress internals
recommendation.body: Keep intentional final assistant text deliverable by default, but suppress commentary, reasoning, unphased pre-tool/inter-tool text, and cron reasoning payloads with focused source and channel regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current delivery-contract lines and docs restored in the latest current-main history point to this owner for deciding the compatibility/security tradeoff.
